NSE IFSC Ltd and the London Stock Exchange have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore strategic collaboration across listings, trading, new products and market connectivity, in a move aimed at strengthening capital-market links between India’s GIFT City and London. The agreement, announced at GIFT IFSC in Gandhinagar on October 13, will allow the two exchanges to explore opportunities for dual and cross-listings across equities, fixed income and exchange-traded funds. The partnership will also look at trading in existing financial products and the development of new products, including derivatives on NSEIX using FTSE Russell indices as underlying references. The MoU also covers possible joint development of new equity indices, cross-border trading connectivity and market-data distribution. The framework is exploratory at this stage, but it signals a deeper push to connect Indian issuers and investors with London’s capital market ecosystem. For NSEIX, the pact comes at a time when GIFT City is being developed as India’s international financial services hub. The exchange already offers a range of products, including Indian single-stock derivatives, index derivatives, currency derivatives, depository receipts and global stocks. It also provides primary-market products such as equity share listings, SPACs, REITs, InvITs, depository receipts, debt securities and ESG debt securities under the IFSCA framework. Live Events V Balasubramaniam, MD and CEO of NSEIX, said the collaboration had emerged from the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, which is aimed at opening new areas in capital-market connectivity and financial-services integration between London and India. "The LSEG London Stock Exchange and NSEIX have taken this first step towards collaborations through dual listings and cross listings across products and exploring a cross-border connect between the two exchanges to provide seamless bidirectional trading opportunities, leading to higher liquidity and a larger pool of investors," Balasubramaniam said. The Securities and Exchange Board of India ( Sebi ) is likely to issue guidelines on the settlement-price mechanism for derivatives on expiry days within about a week, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday. The regulator is examining feedback on its consultation paper following a review of the Closing Auction Session (CAS). “Following review of the Closing Auction Session, a consultation paper was put out to address concerns in respect of settlement price of derivatives on expiry-day. We are currently examining the comments and hope to issue guidelines in about a week’s time,” Pandey said at the second Capital Market Confluence 2026, organised by the Bombay Stock Exchange Brokers’ Forum in Mumbai. The CAS review is part of Sebi’s broader efforts to deepen India’s cash markets, improve price discovery and enhance market efficiency. Pandey said wider participation, stronger securities borrowing and lending, and efficient hedging and arbitrage could help improve liquidity and the functioning of cash markets. In his address, titled “From Regulation to Global Leadership: Positioning India’s Capital Markets as a Standard-Setter for the Next Decade”, the Sebi chairman outlined four broad priorities for the market regulator: proportionate regulation, deeper cash markets, easier access to Indian markets and greater technological resilience. On the regulatory front, Pandey said Sebi was reviewing the Depositories and Participants Regulations to simplify rules and strengthen fraud prevention. The regulator is also exploring a graded compliance framework for stock brokers based on their scale, client exposure and dependence on technology. Live Events “One size need not fit all,” he said. Sebi is also addressing gaps in the interoperability framework for certain transactions, including tender offers, buybacks and offers for sale (OFS). These transactions currently require parallel clearing arrangements, adding to costs and compliance requirements, Pandey said. The regulator is targeting implementation of the proposed changes by the end of November 2026. The move is expected to improve capital efficiency and lower compliance costs while preserving settlement safety, he said. FII selloff has intensified in October, with foreign investors net selling Indian equities worth Rs 45,125 crore in just six sessions in October so far, nearly the same as the total Rs 45,536 crore outflows recorded in the entire month of September. Analysts have listed factors that could change the trend and ease pressure on the market. The Indian stock market snapped a record eight-week-long losing streak last week, ending with gains despite strong upswings and downswings. Yet, FIIs remained bearish and continued selling Indian equities in every session so far in October. The foreign investors have remained net sellers of Indian equities for 11 consecutive sessions since mid-September. What's behind the massive FII outflows? The sharp FII selloff came as bond yields soared to multi-year highs, making the risk-free returns from the debt market more lucrative than equities. The 10-year US Treasury yield recorded its biggest quarterly increase of the 21st century in the three months ended September, Reuters reported. The yield on 10-year US Treasuries climbed above 5.3%, surpassing its 2007 peak and hitting its highest since early 2002. The 30-year yield has touched 5.6%, also not seen since 2002. VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, noted that the rapid acceleration in FII outflows in October so far has taken the total FPI equity selling in 2026 to a whopping Rs 3,60,952 crore. “This massive FPI selling is the primary reason why the Indian market is underperforming this year with negative 13.87% Nifty returns so far in 2026,” he said. The NSE circular stated that no contracts for new expiry months in Polycab India will be issued after the expiry of existing contract months. New strikes will also be introduced in these existing contract months. Read Today's Paper Tata Elxsi Q2 Results: Profit rises 10% YoY to Rs 170 crore; revenue grows 15% SECTIONS Tata Elxsi Q2 Results: Profit rises 10% YoY to Rs 170 crore; revenue grows 15% By Akash Podishetti , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 13, 2026, 06:15:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Tata Elxsi reported a 10% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 170 crore in Q2, while revenue from operations grew 15% to Rs 1,056 crore. Higher employee and operating expenses, along with lower other income, weighed on margins. Net profit for the first half of FY27 rose 14%. ETMarkets.com Tata Elxsi on Tuesday reported a 10% year-on-year (YoY) rise in net profit for the September quarter, helped by double-digit growth in revenue even as higher employee and operating costs kept profit growth below the top-line expansion. The company’s net profit for the quarter ended September stood at Rs 170 crore, compared with Rs 155 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations rose 15% YoY to Rs 1,056 crore from Rs 918 crore a year earlier. Total income from operations, including other income, increased 13% to Rs 1,090 crore, compared with Rs 967 crore a year earlier. Other income fell to Rs 35 crore from Rs 49 crore, partly weighing on the overall profit growth. Profit before tax rose 11% to Rs 239 crore from Rs 215 crore in the year-ago quarter. Total tax expense increased to Rs 69 crore from Rs 60 crore. There was no exceptional item in the quarter. The company’s total expenses grew 13% YoY to Rs 851 crore from Rs 752 crore. Employee benefit expenses, the largest cost item for the company, rose 15% to Rs 620 crore from Rs 539 crore. Other expenses also increased 15% to Rs 131 crore from Rs 114 crore. Cost of materials consumed rose marginally to Rs 73 crore from Rs 72 crore. Depreciation and amortisation expense stood at Rs 24 crore, compared with Rs 23 crore a year earlier. Finance costs declined to Rs 3.57 crore from Rs 4 crore. Live Events Also read: Reliance Jio said to see over $20 billion bids as investors line up for India's biggest IPO The company’s profit before tax margin on revenue from operations stood at 22.7%, compared with 23.4% a year earlier. Net profit margin also moderated to 16.1% from 16.9%, reflecting the impact of higher costs and lower other income. Net profit for the six-month period increased 14% to Rs 341 crore, compared with Rs 299 crore in the same period last year. Profit before tax for the April-September period rose 15% to Rs 472 crore from Rs 411 crore. Total income from operations stood at Rs 2,153 crore, up 13% from Rs 1,897 crore a year earlier.
